title: GCG Text Suffix Attacks on Vision-Language Models: Does the Image Modality Affect Optimization Efficiency?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: VLMs are increasingly deployed and understanding multimodal attack surfaces is important, but the specific question of whether a benign image changes text-space GCG optimization is somewhat niche.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: GCG optimization is compute-intensive and requires understanding gradient-based discrete optimization. Running GCG on a VLM (LLaVA-1.6-7B) adds multimodal complexity. Far beyond beginner CS student capabilities.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: GCG optimization requires many iterations (hundreds) and is computationally expensive. Running this under two conditions on 30 prompts and measuring convergence is a substantial undertaking within 30 hours.

evidence: Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt (BAP, 2025) attacks combine visual overlays and textual cues for VLM jailbreaks, studying the interaction between modalities.
Universal and Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on VLMs (Feb 2026, arXiv:2602.01025) directly addresses VLM-specific jailbreak methodology.
GCG-based image attacks adapt the GCG loss to optimize adversarial images instead of text suffixes, showing the image modality is already being studied as an alternative attack surface.

The specific question of whether a benign image's presence changes text-space GCG optimization efficiency is a narrow variant not directly answered, but the broader VLM jailbreak landscape is active and partially overlapping.
